title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 133-135): u is an automorphism (of 'Galois type') of a profinite group containing π̂_{0,3}, the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞} (free profinite on two generators). That group is an extension of the symmetry group 𝔖_3 (generated by the order-3 rotation ρ and the transposition σ_∞) by π̂_{0,3}; ε_0 = σ_∞ρ. The previous page writes [u,ρ]=int(g) and [u,σ_∞]=int(h), and notes that (g,h) determine u. The 'loop relation' (compatibility of u with the loop/inertia structure) was written u(ε_0)=int(g_0)ε_0^p, with u(l_0)=int(g_0) l_0^p and p in Ẑ^×.

This page only changes notation, for later convenience.
(i) g_0 is renamed f_0, since g and g_0 play quite different roles.
(ii) The multiplier p is renamed μ, Greek initial of 'multiplicateur'. The note says the earlier letter 'is not a happy choice' because it will be needed for characteristics; the transcription renders that letter as ρ, but the previous page and the context show it is p.
(iii) f_0 is replaced by f_0^{-1}, so that the symmetry between the roles of ρ and σ_∞ shows more clearly.
(iv) Likewise the earlier definition h_0 = g_0^{-1}σ_∞(g_0) (§13, (65)) is to become h_0 = g_0 σ_∞(g_0)^{-1}, 'in harmony with' ξ = λρ(λ)^{-1} (a coboundary-type convention).

Result: (5) u(ε_0)=int(f_0^{-1})ε_0^μ, with f_0 in π̂_{0,3} and μ in Ẑ^*; and (6) u(l_0)=int(f_0^{-1}) l_0^μ, which follows at once.

The next page transports these to the indices 1 and ∞ with f_1=ρ(f_0)g^{-1}. It sets μ-1=2ν and arrives at fhσ_∞(gρ(f)^{-1}) = l_0^ν. This is the derivation of relations of Grothendieck-Teichmüller type, with ν playing the role of Drinfeld's m=(λ-1)/2.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page; it is purely notational. The convention switches (f_0 to f_0^{-1}, h_0 to its 'coboundary' form) are internally consistent with (8) on the next page.

ideas.what: Loop relation u(ε_0)=int(f^{-1})ε_0^μ: an automorphism acts on the inertia (loop) generator by conjugation of its μ-th power, with μ the cyclotomic multiplier.
ideas.modern_name: Inertia/cyclotomic condition defining the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group (λ,f), with σ(x)=x^{χ(σ)} up to conjugation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld 1990 (GT); Ihara (profinite GT, early 1990s); Grothendieck, Esquisse (1984) programmatically
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the Teichmüller tower and Galois action; the explicit loop equation is in the Longue Marche continuation notes (unpublished)

ideas.what: Normalizing the cocycle conventions (f vs f^{-1}; h_0 = g_0σ_∞(g_0)^{-1} analogous to ξ=λρ(λ)^{-1}) to make the ρ/σ_∞ symmetry visible.
ideas.modern_name: Choice of sign/cocycle convention for GT pairs

deep.surprise_reason: A notation-only page: renaming g_0 to f_0, the multiplier to μ, inverting f_0, and harmonizing a coboundary convention. Its interest lies only as context for the next page's derivation of GT-type relations, which is itself fairly well known historically as Grothendieck's anticipation of GT.
transcription_corrections: '357' is a marginal page number, not part of the text.
In 'La lettre ρ pour un multiplicateur' the image is more plausibly 'p' (matching the previous page's u(ε_0)=int(g_0)ε_0^p), with the stated reason being that p will be needed for characteristics.
Formula (6) reads u(l_0)=int(f_0^{-1}) l_0^μ (l_0 = ℓ_0), not u(h_0)=... h_0^μ.
A crossed-out label '(5)' or '(B)' stands next to the first formula u(ε_0)=int(f_0)ε_0^μ, with a struck-out tail after it.
The final line reads 'tout ce qui se déduit aussitôt ...', with a struck-out 'plutôt ... d'où découle aussitôt' before (6).
